study.question: Does the small full-versus-counts click-AUC gap persist when auxiliary heads receive the same uniform pooled-history representation, leaving membership grouping only in the primary scorer normalization population?
study.hypothesis: The full-membership advantage may depend on the auxiliary feedback representation and its downstream shared-context training trajectory, rather than on membership-dependent primary scorer moments alone. At a fixed state click reads only the uniform pooled stratum; the auxiliary heads read complementary feedback strata. Cross full/counts grouping with native/uniform auxiliary readout to localize these routes. This is a representation intervention, not a change to labels, historical actions, loss weights, or explicit gradient gates. Prior feedback Dice-input detachment reduced both AUCs but left the full-minus-counts gap positive; it did not establish a uniquely useful feedback-gradient route.

nearest_work.difference: DIN primary text lines 260-277 describes target-conditioned unnormalized pooling and lines 317-335 describes Dice batch/running moments. Inherit those adapted components; test a parameter-free membership-by-auxiliary-readout factorial inside the existing four-task model. No original-method reproduction or novelty claim.
Pinned Dice uses nonaffine BatchNorm1d and learned alpha. Leave it completely unchanged; vary which already-computed pooled vector auxiliary heads consume.

Pinned benchmark forward lines 123-170 initializes separate masked task sequence hubs and exchanges information through layers. Here retain the incumbent union of auxiliary memberships and existing modules, varying auxiliary readout at fixed primary scorer population. This does not implement INFNet or test separate task-specific hubs.

inherited_components: Full incumbent source and config g1-r0080-membership_full_control and byte-identical counts source g1-r0080-membership_counts_control
Action-aware target local activation, 10 temporal blocks, union-membership/complement rows, support folding and native Dice
All target-match/position/block/curvature summaries, adapters, product context modules and task towers
Joint four-task BCE and occupied-cycle auxiliary-context surrogate VJP; this inherited backward is not the ordinary derivative of the reported joint BCE
study.proposed_difference: In two standalone replacements, add one architecture flag and set auxiliary feedback = uniform.detach() during training and uniform during evaluation, immediately after native feedback pooling. Keep original pooling/scoring execution and buffers even when the feedback result is unused. Cross this readout replacement with full versus counts-only compression. Native arms are byte-identical archival references.
predictions: Native full/counts bridges should reproduce click AUC 0.6689612705559688 / 0.668900839165076 at the fixed seed, subject to host reproducibility; these reruns are not independent seed evidence.

If auxiliary readout mediates the advantage, D_uniform=AUC(full,uniform)-AUC(counts,uniform) will be smaller than D_native=0.0000604313908928; predeclared interaction I=D_native-D_uniform should be positive. A useful discriminating observation is D_uniform at most zero, conditional on valid negative-control diagnostics; no single-seed significance claim.

If D_uniform remains close to D_native, the changed auxiliary base is insufficient to explain the gap; remaining utility is consistent with the primary normalization-population route and its coupled training dynamics, not proof of a unique moment mechanism.

Counts/native and counts/uniform pooled bases are equal in real arithmetic because occupied feedback means equal their block uniform mean and counts partition the total. BF16 split-sum rounding can break exact equality; material trajectory differences undermine clean localization.

No trainable parameters or new state should be added: expected 32192421 total, 31793216 embedding, 399205 dense in every arm. At common weights and buffers click predictions must agree between native/uniform readouts within each membership condition, in train and eval with state reset.
falsifiers: I at most zero, an unresolved counts negative-control discrepancy, or a gap unstable under authorized paired seeds undermines the auxiliary-readout mediation hypothesis.

A full/counts difference appearing only as an auxiliary AUC tradeoff does not answer click conditional utility; full failing to exceed counts/permutation controls undermines useful event-assignment evidence.
Changed module state, labels/actions, valid-event exposure, parameter count, host recipe or inherited gradient ownership invalidates the intended contrast.

Even positive I does not establish incremental input information: task masks are derived from supplied action codes, and current results concern representation and optimization under this offline protocol.
alternative_explanations: Fixed-seed optimization variation, adaptivity across validation rounds, and BF16 reassociation can be larger than a 0.00006 AUC gap.

Membership-dependent primary moments, running-state evolution, shared item/scorer gradients and inherited context surrogate VJP can interact with auxiliary private learning; this is not a natural-mediation identification experiment.
Changing auxiliary base alters its task prediction difficulty and context cotangents even though labels and gradient gates remain fixed.
Union masks discard individual task distinctions; counts remain in emptiness patterns. Neither result establishes the utility of every individual task mask.
Official offline delayed feedback, whole-window vocabularies and static snapshots limit temporal and production generalization.

validation_plan.local: AST/syntax, exact archival bridge hashes, method-level source diffs, architecture config matching and study-schema checks only. No torch execution, installation, training or withheld scoring.
host_preflight_required: Instantiate each module with feature_map and its config. Verify parameter and buffer names/shapes, initialization tensors and RNG state agree with its archival parent.

At common weights/buffers, compare native/uniform arms with reset running state in both train and eval. Click predictions and primary scorer buffers must agree; only auxiliary base/readout may differ.

Verify uniform replacement is detached during training: no auxiliary loss gradient to item/action embeddings or scorer. All auxiliary private modules and inherited shared-context transfer remain active. Four finite probabilities, joint BCE and finite backward required.

Use empty, one-event, full, partial and noncontiguous histories. Invalid item/action/mask perturbations must not change predictions. Keep original empty scorer rows and validity filtering; do not expose padded events.

For counts-native versus counts-uniform, report max/RMS pooled-base discrepancy in actual BF16 and optional FP32 diagnostic, same-state prediction discrepancy and one-step gradients. Any diagnostic costs are charged. Do not claim exact parity from algebra.
validation_plan.metrics: Primary full-population validation click AUC and logloss; all four AUC/logloss and auxiliary mean, parameters, allocated GPU/wall/train seconds, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 batch latency at fixed batch. Use host authorized history-length slices with sample/positive/negative counts; no new bins selected from validation outcomes.
validation_plan.interaction: D_native=AUC(full,native)-AUC(counts,native); D_uniform=AUC(full,uniform)-AUC(counts,uniform); I=D_native-D_uniform. Report all values, failures and cost, including if no candidate improves incumbent.

trajectory_interpretation.initial: DIN click AUC 0.6555441 establishes adapted reference, not exact DIN paper reproduction. Strongest imported full utility reference is 0.6689613.
trajectory_interpretation.membership: Blind 0.6684079 loses 0.0005534; counts 0.6689008 and valid-rank permutation 0.6688853 recover most of that difference. Full-versus-counts advantage is only 0.0000604. Counts and permutation do not prove independent incremental input information.
trajectory_interpretation.abandoned_weighting: Equal occupied-stratum weighting gives full 0.6688608 and counts 0.6689491, reversing the gap to -0.00008838. Native membership advantage depends on representation/readout choices.
trajectory_interpretation.latest_backward: Feedback Dice-input detachment gives full 0.6684787 and counts 0.6683928, both worse than native, with positive gap 0.00008585. I_gate=D_native-D_blocked=-0.00002542, opposite the direction expected if this gate removed the full-membership advantage. This fails to support a uniquely helpful feedback-input backward explanation, while not refuting all normalization mechanisms.
trajectory_interpretation.repetitions: Repeated native scores are bit-identical at the same host seed; no independent seed confirmation or uncertainty interval is present.
